Charging by Friction, Contact and Induction

Step 1 of 6
Predict first
Experimental controls
Key features (tap one)
How the three ways of charging compare
FrictionContactInduction
What gets chargedTwo different insulators, rubbed against each other (an amber rod and fur)An uncharged conductor (a metal sphere)An uncharged conductor (a metal sphere)
Do they touch?Yes: they are rubbed togetherYes: the charged conductor touches itNo: the charged object is only brought close
Which electrons move, and whereElectrons go from one insulator to the otherFree electrons go between the charged conductor and the uncharged oneFree electrons flow between the conductor and the Earth, through the earth wire
Earth wire needed?NoNoYes: connected, then removed while the charged object is still near
Charge gainedThe two insulators gain equal and opposite chargesThe same sign as the charged conductorThe opposite sign to the charged object
  • In all three, only electrons move from one object to another. The number of protons does not change.
  • Charge is not created or destroyed: an object becomes negative by gaining electrons, and positive by losing them.
